introduction: The Flexible Resource Selectors spec adds a cross-cutting resolver layer to the apikit project that allows API endpoints and CLI commands to accept human-friendly identifiers (username, email, org slug) in addition to UUIDs for user and organization resources, resolving them transparently to canonical UUIDs before delegating to existing handlers.

glossary.Executor: The db interface type already defined in internal/handlers/ that both resolveUserID and resolveOrgID accept as their database parameter
glossary.OpenMemory: A helper function from the database_layer spec that opens an in-memory SQLite database for use in tests
glossary.WriteAPIError: A helper function used by handlers to write a structured JSON error response with a given HTTP status code and message
glossary.akc: The apikit CLI binary built with Cobra that wraps the Go SDK
glossary.cli_resolve.go: A file in the root apikit package containing the now-redundant resolveOrgSlugFromJSON function and its tests, not owned by any active spec
glossary.detection heuristic: The three-step logic used to classify a selector: (1) if it parses as a UUID, query by id; (2) if it contains '@', query by email; (3) otherwise, query by username or slug
glossary.idx_users_email: The UNIQUE index added to the users.email column by the schema migration introduced in this spec
glossary.orgs: The SQLite table storing organization records including id, slug, and other org fields
glossary.resolveOrgID: Helper function in internal/handlers/ that accepts a selector string and returns the canonical org UUID by querying the database using the detection heuristic
glossary.resolveOrgSlugFromJSON: A client-side org slug resolution function in the root apikit package's cli_resolve.go file that becomes redundant once server-side resolution is implemented and must be deleted
glossary.resolveUserID: Helper function in internal/handlers/ that accepts a selector string and returns the canonical user UUID by querying the database using the detection heuristic
glossary.schema.go: The Go source file in the database layer package that contains the SQL schema creation statement used when initializing a new database
glossary.selector: A string value passed as a path parameter that may be a UUID, username, email address, or org slug — the resolver determines which type it is and returns the canonical UUID
glossary.slug: A human-readable, URL-safe string identifier for an organization (e.g. 'acme-corp'), stored in the orgs table
glossary.two-ID endpoint: An API endpoint that contains two path parameters identifying different resource types, such as PUT /orgs/{id}/members/{user_id}
glossary.users: The SQLite table storing user records including id, username, email, and other profile fields

requirements.title: Database migration: unique index on users.email

user_story.goal: have the server enforce uniqueness of email addresses at the database level
user_story.benefit: email can serve as an unambiguous selector for user resolution

acceptance_criteria.action: execute CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_email ON users(email) and update the schema creation statement in schema.go to include this index for new databases
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: migration completes without error; server proceeds to start normally
acceptance_criteria.trigger: the server starts and runs the schema migration

acceptance_criteria.action: query for all email values appearing more than once, log a FATAL message listing each offending email address and its row count, then exit with a non-zero exit code
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: server exits with non-zero code; log output contains each duplicate email and its count in the format 'FATAL migration failed: duplicate emails detected — deduplicate before restarting: <email> (<N> rows)'
acceptance_criteria.error_condition: the users table contains rows with duplicate email values, causing the CREATE UNIQUE INDEX statement to fail

acceptance_criteria.action: never automatically deduplicate or modify user rows to resolve duplicate email conflicts — the operator must resolve duplicates manually

edge_cases.action: create the idx_users_email unique index without error and proceed with startup
edge_cases.return_contract: migration succeeds; server starts normally
edge_cases.trigger: the server starts on a fresh database with no existing users

edge_cases.action: the IF NOT EXISTS clause allows the statement to succeed even if the index already exists; server proceeds normally
edge_cases.return_contract: migration succeeds; server starts normally
edge_cases.trigger: the server starts on an existing database where all email values are already unique

edge_cases.action: log all offending email addresses in a single FATAL message before exiting
edge_cases.return_contract: server exits with non-zero code; all duplicate emails are listed in the log output
edge_cases.error_condition: multiple distinct email addresses are duplicated (e.g. both alice@example.com and bob@example.com appear more than once)

correctness_properties.title: UUID selectors are always identity-resolved
correctness_properties.for_any: valid UUID string that exists in the users or orgs table
correctness_properties.invariant: resolveUserID or resolveOrgID returns that exact UUID unchanged, producing the same result as the pre-change inline uuid.Parse() + WHERE id = ? pattern

correctness_properties.title: Detection heuristic is unambiguous and deterministic
correctness_properties.invariant: the detection heuristic assigns exactly one classification (UUID, email, or fallback) and always queries exactly one column — there is no case where two columns are queried for the same selector

correctness_properties.title: Not-found always returns sql.ErrNoRows, never a different error
correctness_properties.for_any: selector string that matches no row in the relevant table
correctness_properties.invariant: resolveUserID and resolveOrgID return sql.ErrNoRows (not nil, not a wrapped error, not a custom error type) so that handler error-branching logic is consistent

correctness_properties.title: Org resolver ignores email heuristic
correctness_properties.invariant: resolveOrgID always queries the orgs table by slug, never by email, regardless of whether the selector contains '@'

correctness_properties.title: Migration is idempotent on clean data
correctness_properties.for_any: database where all email values in the users table are unique
correctness_properties.invariant: running the idx_users_email migration any number of times succeeds without error due to the IF NOT EXISTS clause

correctness_properties.title: Duplicate email migration failure is exhaustive
correctness_properties.for_any: database with one or more duplicate email values
correctness_properties.invariant: the migration failure log message lists every email address that appears more than once — no offending address is silently omitted

correctness_properties.title: Backward compatibility: UUID callers are unaffected
correctness_properties.for_any: existing API call or CLI invocation that passes a valid UUID as the {id} or {user_id} parameter
correctness_properties.invariant: the HTTP response is identical to the response that would have been returned before this spec was implemented

execution_paths.title: User endpoint resolved by username end-to-end

steps.action: runs 'akc admin users show alice' where 'alice' is a username
passes the string 'alice' as the user identifier to the Go SDK GetUserByID method
sends GET /users/alice to the apikit server
routes the request to the user handler, extracting 'alice' as the {id} path parameter
calls resolveUserID(h.db, 'alice'); the detection heuristic determines 'alice' is not a UUID and contains no '@', so it queries the users table by username
executes SELECT id FROM users WHERE username = 'alice', finds a matching row, and returns the canonical UUID
uses the returned UUID for all subsequent queries and returns the user resource as JSON
deserializes the HTTP 200 response and returns the User struct to the CLI
prints the user details to stdout

execution_paths.title: Org member endpoint resolved by slug and email end-to-end

steps.action: runs 'akc admin orgs members add acme-corp alice@example.com' where 'acme-corp' is an org slug and 'alice@example.com' is a user email
passes 'acme-corp' and 'alice@example.com' as positional arguments to the Go SDK AddOrgMember method
sends PUT /orgs/acme-corp/members/alice@example.com to the apikit server
routes the request to the org member handler, extracting 'acme-corp' as {id} and 'alice@example.com' as {user_id}
calls resolveOrgID(h.db, 'acme-corp'); the detection heuristic determines 'acme-corp' is not a UUID, so it queries the orgs table by slug
executes SELECT id FROM orgs WHERE slug = 'acme-corp', finds a matching row, and returns the canonical org UUID
calls resolveUserID(h.db, 'alice@example.com'); the detection heuristic finds '@' and queries the users table by email
executes SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = 'alice@example.com', finds a matching row, and returns the canonical user UUID
uses both resolved UUIDs to insert the membership record and returns HTTP 200
prints success confirmation to stdout

execution_paths.title: Server startup migration with duplicate emails — failure path

steps.action: starts the apikit server against a database that contains duplicate email values in the users table
attempts to execute CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_users_email ON users(email)
the statement fails; migration code queries SELECT email, COUNT(*) FROM users GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 to identify offending addresses
logs a FATAL message listing each duplicate email and its row count
exits with a non-zero exit code; the server does not start
sends GET /users/nobody@example.com to the apikit server where no user has that email
routes the request to the user handler, extracting 'nobody@example.com' as the {id} path parameter
calls resolveUserID(h.db, 'nobody@example.com'); the detection heuristic finds '@' and queries the users table by email
executes SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = 'nobody@example.com', finds no matching row, and returns sql.ErrNoRows
detects sql.ErrNoRows and calls WriteAPIError with status 404 and message 'user not found'
returns HTTP 404 with JSON body {error: 'user not found'} to the caller

error_handling.condition: resolveUserID or resolveOrgID finds no matching row for the given selector
error_handling.behavior: the calling handler invokes WriteAPIError with HTTP 404 and the message 'user not found' or 'organization not found' respectively

error_handling.condition: resolveUserID or resolveOrgID returns a database error that is not sql.ErrNoRows
error_handling.behavior: the calling handler invokes WriteAPIError with HTTP 500 and the message 'internal server error'

error_handling.condition: the idx_users_email migration fails because the users table contains duplicate email values
error_handling.behavior: the server queries for all duplicate emails, logs a FATAL message listing each offending email and its row count, and exits with a non-zero exit code without starting

error_handling.condition: the idx_users_email migration fails due to a database error unrelated to duplicate emails
error_handling.behavior: the server logs the error and exits with a non-zero exit code

error_handling.condition: on a two-ID member endpoint, resolveOrgID returns sql.ErrNoRows
error_handling.behavior: the handler returns HTTP 404 with 'organization not found' without attempting to resolve the user selector

error_handling.condition: on a two-ID member endpoint, the org resolves successfully but resolveUserID returns sql.ErrNoRows
error_handling.behavior: the handler returns HTTP 404 with 'user not found'

symbols.name: Parse
symbols.notes: Used in the detection heuristic to determine if a selector is a UUID; returns a non-nil error if the string is not a valid UUID

symbols.name: ErrNoRows
symbols.signature: var ErrNoRows = errors.New("sql: no rows in result set")
symbols.notes: Sentinel error returned by resolveUserID and resolveOrgID when no matching row is found; handlers branch on this value to return HTTP 404
